record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let A be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Do there exist rational functions X and F, with X a Galois covering and X∘A = F∘X, such that for every rational function B of degree at least two the following are equivalent: (i) for every n ≥ 1, the field C(A^{∘n}) ∩ C(B) contains a non-constant rational function, and (ii) B is a compositional right factor of X∘A^{∘ℓ} for some ℓ ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. Let A be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist rational functions X and F such that X is a Galois covering, the diagram (14) ... commutes, and for a rational function B of degree at least two all fields (13) contain a non-constant rational function if and only if B is a compositional right factor of X ∘ A^{∘ℓ} for some l ≥ 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers. A rational function is an element of $\mathbb{C}(z)$, and for rational functions $U,V$ we write $U\circ V$ for their composition and $U^{\circ n}$ for the $n$-fold self-composition of $U$. For a non-constant rational function $U$, let $\mathbb{C}(U)\subset\mathbb{C}(z)$ denote the subfield generated by $U$ over $\mathbb{C}$. A rational function $X\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ is called a Galois covering if the field extension $\mathbb{C}(z)/\mathbb{C}(X)$ is Galois. A rational function $B$ of degree at least two is a compositional right factor of a rational function $H$ if there exists a rational function $C$ with $H=C\circ B$.

A rational function is called special if it is either a Lattès map (a rational function semiconjugate to a multiplication map on an elliptic curve via a finite-to-one holomorphic map), or, up to conjugation by a Möbius transformation, a power map $z\mapsto z^{\pm n}$ or a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$.

Let $A\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Determine whether there exist rational functions $X,F\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ with $X$ a Galois covering and
$$X\circ A \;=\; F\circ X,$$
such that for every rational function $B\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ of degree at least two the following two conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every integer $n\geq 1$, the intersection $\mathbb{C}(A^{\circ n})\cap \mathbb{C}(B)$ contains a non-constant rational function.
\item There exists an integer $\ell\geq 0$ such that $B$ is a compositional right factor of $X\circ A^{\circ \ell}$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is a conjecture by Pakovich on a right-factor characterization tied to Galois coverings and semiconjugacies of non-special rational functions. Web searches return Pakovich's related papers on amenable semigroups, tame rational functions, and intersections of lemniscates, but no source establishes the conjecture in full generality. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses amenable semigroups of rational functions and related compositional structures, but does not resolve the right-factor characterization conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work by the same author; the conjecture is not stated as a theorem here.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates
status_evidence.snippet: Studies decompositions of iterates of rational functions and intersections of fields generated by them under tameness assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results in the tame case but does not settle the general non-special conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Fedor Pakovich personal page
status_evidence.snippet: Lists publications on semigroups, semiconjugacies, and decompositions of rational functions.
status_evidence.claim: No publication listed announces a proof of the conjecture in full.
